name: sc
description: SwarmCloud from inside a Claude Code session. Two skills: `sc` reads the cluster -- the account pool and its quota windows, which pool actually binds each runner profile, what is running, what is wrong -- and never writes. `delegate` owns the decision to run work remotely instead of locally, dispatches it by runner-profile NAME from the frozen catalogue, reports a failure as something actionable rather than a task id, and brings the result back into the working tree. It writes, so it says when it asks first. Five agents and a workflow run a Claude Code workflow's steps in SwarmCloud while each still shows as a running row: `sc:remote` runs one step remotely, and `/sc:swarmcloud` runs a whole SwarmCloud workflow spec with an `sc:step` row per step, gives each single dispatched task an `sc:task` row, and `sc:wait` spaces a row's retries while the bridge is down. `/sc check` reports this project's stuck or stale SwarmCloud work that THIS Claude Code session started (every submission is tagged with the session; other sessions' work in the same tenant is never a candidate) and attaches rows for its running workflows that have none, and `/sc watch` runs that check every 30 minutes (CronCreate), re-armed by the SessionStart hook and armed by itself whenever the session attaches to or starts SwarmCloud work, unless `/sc watch off` was saved for the project. `delegate` works through the plugin's own MCP server, which fetches the swarm-mcp bridge from GitHub at the tag matching this version and needs only uv. The `sc` skill and /sc run `uv run sc` in the session's directory, so they need a checkout of this repository.

deployment_url.title: SwarmCloud deployment URL
deployment_url.description: The address of YOUR SwarmCloud deployment -- the load balancer for a team deployment (e.g. https://swarm.example.com), or the *.run.app address for a solo one. Your platform operator knows it.

oauth_client_id.title: OAuth client ID (Desktop app)
oauth_client_id.description: The deployment's Desktop app OAuth client ID (ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com). Your operator creates one per deployment and allowlists it on IAP; with it you sign in as yourself with `sc login`. Leave empty for a solo deployment without IAP.

oauth_client_secret.title: OAuth client secret (Desktop app)
oauth_client_secret.description: The secret of that same Desktop app OAuth client (starts GOCSPX-). Stored in your system's secure credential store, never in settings.json. Leave empty for a solo deployment without IAP.

default_target.title: Default target for dispatched work
default_target.description: Where the dispatching tools send work when a call does not say: cloud (dispatch it to SwarmCloud), local (send nothing; the work runs in this session), or hybrid (a unit that names a runner profile goes to the cloud unless the call declares needs_local -- filesystem, keychain or interactive -- in which case it stays local). A call's own target overrides this for that call only. Any other value stops the plugin's server at start-up.

auto_attach.title: Show running SwarmCloud workflows and tasks at session start
auto_attach.description: When on, a new or resumed session in which this plugin is configured lists your tenant's SwarmCloud workflows that are still running, and your single tasks that are (read-only, a few seconds at most, silent when none run or SwarmCloud cannot be reached) and is told to run /sc attach --all first, which shows them as live [SwarmCloud] rows. Turn off to start sessions without it; /sc attach --all still works by hand.

tenant.title: Tenant
tenant.description: The tenant every call acts in; empty uses your default: the workspace chosen in Settings › Profile, else your personal workspace when it is ready. Name a group's tenant id here to keep the plugin's tools and its session-start check in that group (the swarm_tenants tool, or `swarm tenants`, lists the tenants you may choose). It reaches the plugin as SWARM_TENANT; a SWARM_TENANT already set in the environment Claude Code was started with wins over this setting.

max_live_rows.title: Live rows followed by /sc attach --all
max_live_rows.description: How many running SwarmCloud workflows, and how many of your running single tasks, /sc attach --all shows as live rows (each workflow's unfinished steps are one row each). Default 100; any value is held to 1-200. The ones a cap leaves out are the ones furthest from finishing, listed with the command that follows each. Claude Code's /workflows panel is its own UI: the plugin cannot add scrolling to it, so every row is one compact line, closest to finish first (steps done of the total, then how long the current step has run), grouped by workspace.
